item.content:encoded:
Chamber 0000501, confirmed to be empty, had one (1) standard Foundation GPS unit placed inside it. When the chamber was sealed, GPS failed. Data from the unit upon retrieval showed that the satellite was unable to confirm source location during this time.

GPSs do not work that way. The satellites send to the GPS, not the other way around.

It seems like they should put a GPS and transmitter in one of the spaces for organs, since they get opened regularly, so they'd be able to find where it is when it opens.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Okay, a few things about the audio file:

A. It links to an outside site. For all I know about computers, that may be unavoidable, but I doubt it. If at all possible, all files, images, links, etc. should be part of the site. Also, if any reader were to actually go to "pleasesendhelp.com", where the mp3 thing appears to be located, they would find what appears to be a half-baked attempt at a webcomic. This would probably break the suspension of disbelief; I know it did for me.

B. The bolded, capslocked warnings are 1. unprofessional and uncomfortable to read and 2. Promise what they can't deliver. Unless you've somehow managed to find an audio file that can do any of that stuff (which I find EXTREMELY unlikely), people are going to be disappointed when it's just some sound that doesn't do anything on its own.
This would really break the suspension of disbelief. You know how those articles about anomalous pictures or have effects when viewed don't actually have the things that are supposed to do anomalous stuff? That's because those anomalies don't actually exist, and it's poor form to basically say "No, really, this is supposed to do things to you!" when you know it won't.

That being said, the audio file itself is really neat and scary and whatnot. It's just not anomalous.

EDIT: I have a migraine now. How the fuck did you do that? (edit: Every damn time!)

EDIT 2: Please make it stop.

item.content:encoded:
I think it has the potential to be a really interesting addition, but not as it is currently and not just with some compartments holding weird things.

Has anyone seen that unfortunate sequel to an amazing flick - Hypercube? The smaller cube cells sometimes had weird environmental effects, like time would slow, gravity would inverse etc. What if some of the compartments had effects on the objects placed inside and some didn't, or some had different effects? What if it was suggested that others had simultaneous access to the compartments? Like opening one combination to find an object, removing and studying the object before returning it, then when going back to it a note saying "stop touching my stuff!" is attached?

I think this one might be one of those entries that benefits from an extended test log to which anyone can submit.
